# Materials {.unnumbered}

Interactive artifacts, handouts, and other student-facing files used in lectures and labs. Items are added here as the semester progresses, and are linked from the relevant [weekly notes](../weeks/w01.qmd) and [lab sheets](../labsheets/lab01.qmd).

| Item | What it is | Used in |
|---|---|---|
| 📽️ [Deck 01 — Logistics](w01-deck-01-logistics.html) | Opening lecture slides: schedule, assessment, tools, and how the course works. (Slide deck — use arrow keys.) | [Week 01](../weeks/w01.qmd) |
| 📽️ [PAGAL: Programming in the Age of AI](w01-pagal-age-of-ai.html) | The PAGAL column in slide form: the Specify–Verify loop, why programming is becoming a commodity, and Computational X — computation as every discipline's second half. | [Week 01](../weeks/w01.qmd) |
| 📽️ [Deck 02 — What is a Computer?](w01-deck-02-what-is-a-computer.html) | Lecture 2 slides: computing vs computer vs programming vs computational thinking; the stored-program dividing line. | [Week 01](../weeks/w01.qmd) |
| 🖨️ [Hello, World — all the way down](w01-hello-under-the-hood.html) | printf, honestly: five instructions (read · write · move · count · check), a finger, and a code book. Act 1 prints “abba” in a two-letter world; Act 2 grows the book to ASCII and prints Hello, world! — same program, bigger data. | [Week 01](../weeks/w01.qmd) |
| 📽️ [Deck 03 — Number Systems](w02-deck-03-number-systems.html) | Week 02 slides: radix-q systems, binary↔decimal conversion, two's complement, fixed point, and IEEE FP32 — ending at “how many bits does a number deserve?” | [Week 02](../weeks/w02.qmd) |
| 🎡 [The Number Playground](w02-number-playground.html) | Three interactive machines: poke 8 bits and watch the decimal form; spin the complement sundial (one pattern, four reading conventions — find the overflow cliff and the double zeros); dissect a live IEEE FP32 bit by bit. | [Week 02](../weeks/w02.qmd) |
| 📽️ [Deck 04 — The Computer, Revisited](w02-deck-04-computer-revisited.html) | Recap of the Week-1 machines, the von Neumann architecture named, and the calculator-vs-computer dividing line: where does the procedure live? | [Week 02](../weeks/w02.qmd) |
| 🧮 [The Toy Computer](w02-toy-computer.html) | A complete von Neumann machine in 40 visible cells: program it in ten instructions, watch fetch–decode–execute narrated, and climb the six-rung ladder from sequencing to the recursion wall. | [Week 02](../weeks/w02.qmd) |
| 🔧 [Under the Hood — Part 1: The Parts](w02-under-the-hood-1-parts.html) | The guided climb, stations 0–3: a switch flipped by a wire (the logical transistor), gates discovered by wiring switches in series and parallel, and a real ripple adder — arithmetic is wiring. | [Week 02](../weeks/w02.qmd) |
| 🔧 [Under the Hood — Part 2: Memory & Time](w02-under-the-hood-2-memory.html) | Stations 4–5: feed a gate its own output and it *remembers* (build a flip-flop from two NOR gates), then the clock — set the bell's rhythm too fast and watch the notebook faithfully record garbage. | [Week 02](../weeks/w02.qmd) |
| 🔧 [Under the Hood — Part 3: The Machine](w02-under-the-hood-3-machine.html) | Stations 6–7: a machine built entirely from your own parts — registers of flip-flops, a control unit that is itself two flip-flops, a hand-cranked clock and live timing diagram — then the ladder back up to `c = a + b;`. | [Week 02](../weeks/w02.qmd) |
| 📦 [lab01.tar.gz](../labs/lab01.tar.gz) | The Lab 01 pack: installer (infers your branch from the machine), starters, and the self-check. Extract, `./install.sh`, follow the [lab sheet](../labsheets/lab01.qmd). | [Lab 01](../labsheets/lab01.qmd) |
| 📽️ [Deck 07 — Types, Assignments & Operators](w03-deck-07-types-operators.html) | W03 Tuesday: the type wardrobe (size + reading convention), `=` as "gets", operator precedence & associativity, promotion/truncation/casts, and six predict-the-output traps. | [Week 03](../weeks/w03.qmd) |
| 📽️ [Deck 05 — Complements & Overflow](w03-deck-05-complements-overflow.html) | W03 Monday: one's & two's complement fully worked, arithmetic with them, and overflow — the silent cliff, from 8-bit examples to Ariane 5. | [Week 03](../weeks/w03.qmd) |
| 📽️ [Deck 06 — Your First C Program](w03-deck-06-first-c-program.html) | W03 Tuesday: hello.c line by line; gcc and ./ annotated word by word; variables as named cells with a reading convention; the integer-division surprise. | [Week 03](../weeks/w03.qmd) |
| 🐢 [The Turtle Computer](w01-turtle-computer.html) | Your first programming language: ten words, one turtle, no typing. Six missions in which each new word is *invented* because a problem demands it — and the reward comes only when the machine's output matches your intention. | [Week 01](../weeks/w01.qmd), Lab 01 |
